The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\). For a prime \(p\), let \(v_p(x)\) be the exponent of \(p\) in \(x\).

When Mark replaces \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), for every prime \(p\), the pair of exponents  
\[
(v_p(a),v_p(b))
\]
is replaced by
\[
(\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b))).
\]
So the multiset of \(p\)-adic valuations on the board is unchanged for each prime \(p\).

A move leaves the board unchanged exactly when one of the two chosen numbers divides the other. Therefore, when Mark finishes, the final numbers form a divisibility chain. Sorting the final numbers increasingly as
\[
x_1\le x_2\le \cdots \le x_{2100},
\]
we have \(x_i\mid x_{i+1}\). Hence for each prime \(p\), the sequence \(v_p(x_i)\) is nondecreasing. Since the multiset of \(p\)-adic valuations is invariant, \(v_p(x_i)\) is simply the \(i\)-th smallest \(p\)-adic valuation among \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

We need \(x_{2026}\). This is the \(75\)-th largest final number, since
\[
2100-2026+1=75.
\]
For a fixed prime \(p\), the number of integers from \(1\) to \(2100\) divisible by \(p^e\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^e}\right\rfloor.
\]
Thus \(v_p(x_{2026})\ge e\) exactly when at least \(75\) of the original numbers have \(p\)-adic valuation at least \(e\). Therefore
\[
v_p(x_{2026})=\max\left\{e\ge 0:\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^e}\right\rfloor\ge 75\right\}.
\]
Since
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^e}\right\rfloor\ge 75
\iff
\frac{2100}{p^e}\ge 75
\iff
p^e\le 28,
\]
we just need the largest power of each prime at most \(28\).

So the relevant prime powers are
\[
2^4=16,\qquad 3^3=27,\qquad 5^2=25,
\]
and the primes
\[
7,11,13,17,19,23
\]
appear to the first power. No prime \(\ge 29\) appears.

Hence the \(2026\)-th smallest final number is
\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]
The number of its positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
